# Hyper-spectral measurements of Terrestrial Mars Analogue with the SPIM facility

S. De Angelis (1), M.C. De Sanctis (1), E. Ammannito (2,1), T. Di Iorio (3), P.Manzari (1)  
(1) Institute for Space Astrophysics and Planetology, IAPS-INAF, Rome Italy, (2) University of California Los Angeles – IGPP (CA-USA), (3) ENEA, UTMEA-TER, Roma, Italy, (simone.deangelis@iaps.inaf.it)

## Introduction

The SPIM facility is a laboratory VIS-IR spectrometer developed to support spaceborne observations of rocky bodies of the Solar System. Currently this laboratory setup is used to support the DAWN mission [1], which is in journey towards the asteroid 1-Ceres, and to support the 2018 Exo-Mars mission in the spectral investigation of Martian subsurface. The main part of this setup is an imaging spectrometer that is a spare of the DAWN Visible InfraRed spectrometer (VIR) [2]. The spectrometer has been assembled and calibrated at Selex ES and installed in the facility developed in the INAF-IAPS laboratory in Rome. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Summary

The SPectral IMaging (SPIM) facility is a laboratory imaging VIS-IR spectrometer, operative in the INAF/IAPS laboratory in Rome. The facility is used as a laboratory support for the DAWN mission (to the asteroids Vesta and Ceres) and for the 2018 ExoMars mission (to Mars). This imaging spectrometer, which is the spare of the VIR spectrometer [1,2] on-board the DAWN spacecraft, is operative in the 0.22-5.05 μm spectral range. It is characterized by high spatial (38 μm) and spectral (2 nm in the VIS channel, 12 nm in the IR channel) resolution. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
